newsitem.title: UK: Errant Catholic bishop wants to marry divorcee.
newsitem.headline: Errant Catholic bishop wants to marry divorcee.

text.p: An errant Catholic bishop who fathered an illegitimate child 15 years ago said in an interview published on Sunday that he intends to marry the divorcee he ran away with but he denied they ever had a sexual relationship.

In a confession to a racy, top-selling British newspaper, for which he received a reported 300,000 pound ($465,900) fee, disgraced Bishop Roderick Wright said he could not fight his feelings for former parishioner Kathleen MacPhee.

"There has been no sexual relationship between us...We have never made love to each other. We have not even shared the same bed or slept together," he told the News of the World. "We tried to contain it. We spent time not seeing each other. There were long gaps."
Wright apologised for the hurt and damage they had caused and said he had never intended to "go missing" when he left his cathedral in Oban, Scotland.
"We were going to start a new life together. That was my hope and plan. But it has spiralled out of control."
The former bishop also regretted neglect and hurt he had caused to his illegitimate son Kevin, the result of his relationship with another woman, Joanna Whibley.
But he denied that there had been other mistresses. "There have been no other affairs with any other women. Just these two.
Wright's startling disclosures were the latest saga in the affair that has shaken the Catholic Church in Britain to the core and thrust the question of celibacy into the headlines.

Church leaders were outraged by the interview and condemned Wright for selling his story to the press. The News of the World, which refused to reveal the fee, said it would be paid to MacPhee's three children.
"We regard the sale of his story by Roderick Wright as deplorable," Cardinal Thomas Winning, head of the Catholic Church in Scotland, said in a statement.
"I feel disgusted," added Father Sean MacAulay, a priest at Wright's former parish.

Wright, 56, resigned as bishop three days after he vanished with MacPhee, 41. The church was still reeling from the scandal when Whibley came forward and disclosed that the errant bishop was the father of her son.

She said she knew that Wright had planned to resign as bishop but she had hoped that he would come and live with her and their child. His disappearance with another women prompted her finally to reveal her guilty secret.
Footage of Kevin sobbing about his absent father on national television saying, "It's too late now. I don't even want him if he comes," added another tragic dimension to a tawdry tale.
Wright said Whibley had every right to say what she did and he wished her and their son happiness.
"I can only say I have a very guilty conscience because of the way I have treated him and because of my negligence," he told the newspaper.
"I only wish him happiness. But at this particular time I don't know how I can bring him his happiness."
Wright described how his relationship with MacPhee started as friendship but grew into something stronger while she was battling cervical cancer.
MacPhee, pictured in a T-shirt holding hands with Wright in the hideaway in northern England, said she hoped there would be a "healing of all the hurt."
Earlier Whibley had appealed to Wright on BBC television to come out of hiding. "I know your turmoil and you deserve a real life and forgiveness without limit," she said.
The bishop's brother, Donald Wright, said he was devastated by the revelations and also appealed to Wright to contact him. ($1=.6439 Pound)
